steps.text: Place carrots in a large pot and cover with salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until carrots are tender, about 15 minutes. Drain carrots in a strainer.
Melt butter in the same pot over medium heat. Stir in brown sugar and honey; reduce heat to medium-low.
Add carrots and stir until evenly coated. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Baby Carrots
raw_recipe.description: These baby sweet carrots cooked with honey, butter, and brown sugar are irresistibly delicious! Made in one pot, they take just 20 minutes to make.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make a perfect holiday side dish: sweet baby carrots. Honey, butter, and brown sugar make these sweet baby carrots irresistible to adults and kids alike! This recipe only needs four ingredients, so it's a quick and easy option at any time of the year. Served warm, these sweet baby carrots are even a delicious snack!
video.name: How to Make Sweet Baby Carrots

review.reviewBody: I'm the author of this recipe...I'm glad so many people are enjoying it. One thing I notice is that many reviewers are saying that 1/2 cup of butter makes too much sauce. It does make a lot of sauce, but the reason for us is that my family likes to dip their bread in the excess sauce to sop it up. Regardless, I'm happy to share one of my family's favorites with you!

Will use this one again with a couple of modifications. We don't need extra sauce to dip bread in so just made half as much sauce as called for and used the 1 lb package of baby carrots. It was plenty. It was a tad sweet so will decrease the honey and brown sugar a bit next time. Also steamed the carrots instead of cooking in water. The flavor and texture were fantastic.

Sooo easy and tasty. I only used 1/4 cup of brown sugar, 3 Tb butter, and 1 Tb honey, and it had plenty of sauce. I used baby carrots, and they were done in 15 min covered. I will definitely be using this recipe in the future. A great way to prepare carrots.

Great recipe! I only had standard carrots on hand.. peeled and cut them into coins, adjusted the cooking time, as they did not require as much time cooking time to soften. Followed others recommendation to make sure the carrots were dried prior to adding the butter/honey/sugar mixture. The only tweak I added was a touch (approx. 1/8 teaspoon) of cayenne pepper. 
Gave the carrots some very mild kick.

Excellent recipe, just what I was hoping it would be. I used 1/4 cup of butter, 3 T brown sugar and 1 T honey, per the suggestion of others, and there was more than enough sauce. I cooked the carrots until they were still slightly firm, drained, and immediately cooled them with cold water because I didn't want them to be too soft. After melting the sauce ingredients back in, I tossed the carrots in the sauce and heated them through.

Although I don't eat butter, I made this glaze for steamed carrots for my husband. I steamed the baby carrots in my steamer and added the glaze. I did change it up a bit after reading a few comments. 3 Tablespoons of butter, 3 Tablespoons of brown sugar, and 1 Tablespoon of honey--with a small extra squirt because he really likes honey. I cut the butter in small pieces, added the brown sugar, and then just threw it in the microwave (covered with plastic wrap) for about 25-35 seconds. After making sure it was well stirred and the brown sugar had disintegrated, I covered the carrots with the glaze. I will be using this recipe from now on! Wonderful!
Second time using this method but I did cut down on the butter and halved (brown) sugar. Family still loved it.

Very yummy. I was short on time so I halved the carrots lengthwise. I also read up in the reviews and used only 1/3 of the sauce mixture. After using a slotted spoon to serve the carrots I was left with maybe 1/4 cup of sauce. So I saved it and I will add it to the next batch that I make. I am going to double the carrots next time because it was so delicious!
I sliced the baby carrots prior to cooking so my 2 year old son can pick them up with his fingers and doubled the ingredients
These were so good! Even the kids loved them. Had the perfect amount of sweetness. I halved the sauce and was the perfect amount.

Delicious! I did cut the sauce way back to 3 Tbsp each of butter and brown sugar and 1 Tbsp of honey. I wanted it to be a little thicker than it was and cling to the carrots more so at the end I made a *tiny* bit of cornstarch slurry and whisked it in. Other than just cutting back the quantity of sauce and thickening it a bit I left the recipe alone and it was absolutely delicious!

I made this 2 days ago and it was great. I did cut the glaze in half and added a bit of vinegar to taste. It was so good the next time I make it, I will double the recipe and use sliced carrots. I ate a lot "tasting" !
Delicious!!! Only thing is, I had too much of the glaze. I’ll cut back at least by a third next time. But the glaze is great on sliced ham, so it’s a win-win!
YUM!
I made the double amount, it seems like a lot of butter to use so I recommend cutting the butter down to half?

Honestly I had never made carrots like this before. Served the as a side with meatloaf and mashed potatoes. My husband is a Navy vet and he said he had not had carrots like this since was in the Navy. He absolutely loved them.
Few ingredients, quick cooking time, delish!

I tried this recipe tonight and it was delicious! I realized just as I was draining the carrots and melting the butter, that I was out of honey. I did have some maple syrup so I added just about a half a teaspoon. It’s a terrific recipe and I plan on making it frequently.
I used carrot chips instead of baby carrots and it worked just as well. Delicious balance of butter and sweet. Not too rich and not too sugary. Definitely keeping this for my candied carrot recipe.
Yummy and easy to make! Great Easter side dish!
